_doc: RO4, OP3, OP4 in design/RimMandrake/operating_requirements_2026-11-01.md. Operations owns this table. routes: first match wins, by fnmatch on an ops_watch metric or alarm key, or a Dispatcher alarm kind. route program = the program contained it, the journal holds it, no incident; role = an incident for `reader`, rising the chain; owner = an incident that starts at him. cause: readings sharing it are one incident. class: for an alarm with no ranges class. readers: who may be filed for, and what wakes them. breaker_emergency is program because its own told row (relentless.breaker_same_cause) is the signal; dry:* because a dry tick writes nothing and its operator reads the alarm. selftest_incident.py fails on a kind this table misses (alarm_census.py reads them from the source) and `rimflow file --for` refuses a reader not here.

policy._doc: chain[0] is the route's reader. ladder: minutes from told_at to chain[2] and chain[3]; chain[1] comes at the reading's ack_within_min. OP4: emergency reaches him at 60 unacked, distressed after 4 h. min_step_min: at least this long on a rung, which is what spaces the rungs after an expired recover_by. event_quiet_min covers a Dispatcher alarm, a reading with no sane value: 7 h clears the 6 h alarm_every_s rate limit, so a repeat is seen. chain entries asking the reader's own role again are skipped (incident.next_rung; an Operations reader goes Operations, Conductor, him, at chain[3]'s minute; INCIDENT_CHAIN_DEDUPE_OPERATIONS_RUNG). runs_per_hour: the Conductor and fresh Operations runs incidents may ask for, shared by all incidents; the reader's own alarm run is held by the role's alarm_run_gap_s and daily limits. owner_revisit_min: an incident at his rung is revisited (a fresh Operations run re-reads it, its ack and plan cleared) this long after it reached him or was last revisited, or at its recover_by if an ack set a later one (OPS_ROLE_DIAGNOSE_STARVED_AT_FOUR_RUNS). A revisit with no news (readings and plan unchanged since the last one, incident.revisit_news; revisit_clock_slack_min: a clock metric only aged if it rose by the status time elapsed, within this) is re-armed with no run and a revisit_quiet row, for at most revisit_quiet_max_min since a run last read it. revisit_batch_min: a run going out takes every revisit due inside this many minutes, so staggered incidents fall into step (an ack whose recover_by lies past the window is untouched) (measured 2026-11-03: revisits came 2 to 15 min apart, each its own run; INCIDENT_REVISIT_TAME_SAME_NEWS_HOURLY). tame_relapses / tame_window_h: a relapse is a closed incident reopened (inside relapse_h); the tame_relapses-th of one cause inside tame_window_h stops it buying full Operations reads and files one structural item, spawned --from structural_from, quoting its acks; it stays open on its ladder (INCIDENT_RELAPSE_TAME_STOP_FULL_READS; plan-20261101164253 was one relapse, then a join).

OWNER.by: the Conductor's sitting; never rung by a program

routes._why: RO1: report-only and coarse, nothing rings; the Conductor reads it in role_use
relentless restore_bundle could not bring a put-down clone's carried commits back into a fresh clone; the bundle stays on disk and the alarm names it (ALARM_ROUTE_FIX_RESTORE_INCOMPLETE_ORPHAN)
relentless_integrity found damage in a clone or item at its gate; the gate journals it every tick and notes it once per distinct damage
relentless_game could not enable the mods a game slot needs; the item is held with the reason (LIVE_MODLIST_ENFORCE_BEFORE_SLOT)
relentless_game routed a game-phase environment cause once to one fixer and held the item (no builder, no new generation)
a blind checker blamed the environment (a named dependency), not the code; relentless withholds the verdict and waits on that dependency
relentless_answer: a legacy owner_call hold with no question_id is never guess-matched; the Conductor answers it with relentless.py unhold
relentless lapse_holds raised; the tick journals it and the steps still run
relentless asked for help on an item and the ask itself failed
OPS_CHURN_MEASURE_RETURNS_ARE_NOT_PROGRESS: churn or a blind instrument is its own cause; under work_belt (open since 2026-11-01) its Conductor line was swallowed the pass it first filed
CHECKER_DEATHS_MONITOR_29_NOBODY_NOTICED: the same cause as checks_lost_items, read as a run broken by verdicts
CHECKER_DEATHS_ALARM_BUILD_29_WENT_UNHEARD: checkers dying across items is one cause on the checker launch; under work_belt an open belt incident would swallow its Conductor line
no target or ranges row yet, so nothing rings; the census reads every point a collector builds, so a row added later lands on a route

as overbudget: on 2026-11-02 role:Operations:overspend_day fell through to role:* and opened a fresh Operations incident run (OPS_OVERSPEND_FIX_ALARM_FEEDS_ITS_METER)

a run winding down (unit gone, scope or marked processes not yet): the supervisor keeps it busy and re-checks every tick, and one that stays so is alarmed as role:*:overtime then stop_failed; as an incident each one-tick sighting reopened roles-20261103041057 (RELAPSE_ROLES_FIX_DIED_TWICE)

relentless_attrib: a repair's fixtures refuse it (instrument_fixture_refused) or cannot print FIXTURE_VERDICT (instrument_fixture_no_verdict), so the waiting item keeps its candidate; unrouted and unseen by the census until INCIDENTS_FIX_ONE_READER_ELEVEN_OPEN taught it `mod.NAME` and `a or b`
as instrument_fixture_*: the dependency an item waits on ended but its check refuses the release
